work packages for Grid Automation products (Protection, Automation &
Control / digital substation portfolio). The role leads planning and
execution for internal engineering teams and coordinates outsourced
engineering partners where they contribute to the scope - ensuring

 Project / Package Execution & SQDC Performance

 Use structured root-cause analysis (logs, test evidence, device behaviour) to drive issue resolution with R&D and partners. 
 Act as the technical interface between QA, development and application engineering to protect release quality.
 Outsourced Partner Coordination

 Stakeholder Management & Communication

 Manage complex and sometimes conflicting priorities with professionalism.
 Leadership, Soft Skills & Team Dynamics

 Engage and motivate teams in a matrix and multicultural context, including teams in other countries

 Strong oral and written communication skills in English;

Dans les logiciels industriels, les cycles de vente s'enlisent lorsque les prospects n'arrivent pas à se projeter dans le produit. À titre de consultant en solutions, vous comblez cet écart : vous créez des démonstrations personnalisées, vous chargez de vraies données clients dans des environnements d'essai et vous traduisez des flux de travail de maintenance complexes en un argumentaire de valeur clair pour les opérateurs, les directeurs d'usine et les dirigeants.

Vous vous joindrez à l'équipe des consultants en solutions de MaintainX à titre de partenaire technique de nos directeurs de comptes du marché intermédiaire. L'équipe prend en charge tout ce qui est technique entre le premier appel et la signature du contrat : découverte, démonstrations, appels d'offres, questionnaires, essais et validation technique.

Vous serez aussi l'expert produit sur qui l'équipe de vente peut compter. Lorsqu'un directeur de comptes a une question technique pointue, c'est vers vous qu'il se tourne. Après chaque lancement de produit, vous tenez la bibliothèque de démonstrations à jour. Lorsqu'un représentant débutant présente l'offre à un nouveau secteur, vous l'aidez à affiner son positionnement.

Le poste

- Mener la découverte avec les directeurs de comptes afin de cartographier les flux de travail, les points de friction et les décideurs de chaque prospect, puis bâtir le plan de démonstration et d'évaluation en conséquence.

- Présenter des démonstrations sur mesure et mener des essais pratiques, en chargeant les données d'actifs du client pour que les parties prenantes voient leur exploitation dans MaintainX.

- Diriger la validation technique et les preuves de concept dans des cycles impliquant de multiples parties prenantes, en répondant avec exactitude aux questions sur le produit, la sécurité et l'intégration pour éviter que les transactions ne s'enlisent.

- Collaborer avec l'équipe des Services professionnels aux intégrations propres à chaque client avec des logiciels tiers, lorsqu'une transaction l'exige.

- Maintenir à jour les démonstrations, le contenu et le matériel de vente à mesure que le produit évolue (environ trois mises à jour par semaine), et encadrer les directeurs de comptes en matière de connaissance du produit et de positionnement.

Vous travaillerez de concert avec les équipes du marketing produit, de la gestion de produit, de l'ingénierie, de l'implantation et du soutien, et vous leur transmettrez ce que vous entendez des clients. Dans six à douze mois, vous soutiendrez les évaluations du marché intermédiaire de bout en bout, les directeurs de comptes vous intégreront tôt aux transactions, et les commentaires clients que vous recueillez contribueront à façonner le produit et les messages.

- 3 ans et plus d'expérience en vente technique, en ingénierie de solutions, en implantation ou en conception de solutions

- Expérience de travail dans les secteurs de la fabrication, des opérations industrielles ou de l'entreposage, ou de vente à ces secteurs, avec une réelle exposition aux flux de travail opérationnels

 Résumé du poste 
 Le poste de Chef, Établissement stratégique des prix consiste à diriger l’établissement des prix pour un ou plusieurs secteurs thérapeutiques (ST) attitrés, en élaborant et en mettant en œuvre la stratégie de prix tout au long du cycle de vie des produits, du lancement et des nouvelles indications jusqu’à l’arrivée des produits génériques. La personne titulaire collabore étroitement avec l’Accès au marché du ST, l’Économie de la santé, les Finances, les Affaires juridiques et l’équipe mondiale afin de protéger l’accès des patients et la valeur commerciale, tout en respectant les exigences du CEPMB et des payeurs. Elle contribue également aux capacités communes d’établissement des prix qui soutiennent tous les ST.
 Responsabilités principales
 Stratégie de prix : Assumer la responsabilité des évaluations de prix pour les actifs attitrés, y compris les options de prix, les scénarios, les analyses de sensibilité et les répercussions sur les prix de liste et nets, et recommander une position de prix.
 Analyses de rentabilité et modélisation des ententes : Diriger l’apport de l’établissement des prix aux analyses de rentabilité de l’accès, y compris la modélisation des prix nets et des ententes, les analyses comparatives et les hypothèses clés; assurer une vigilance à l’égard des prix des produits concurrents et de la réglementation sur les prix afin qu’AbbVie occupe une position concurrentielle, tout en respectant des pratiques d’établissement des prix conformes.
 Négociations avec les payeurs : Élaborer les volets d’établissement des prix de la préparation des négociations avec les payeurs publics et privés, y compris les offres et les contre-offres, l’économie des ententes et les paramètres de négociation; appuyer la direction dans les négociations stratégiques.
 Contrats et conditions commerciales : Examiner les prix et les conditions commerciales dans les lettres d’intention (LI), les ententes d’inscription de produits (EIP), les modifications et les renouvellements.
 Gouvernance et conformité : Gérer les risques liés aux prix, les remontées d’information, les dossiers d’approbation et la mise en œuvre conformément aux exigences du CEPMB et aux politiques internes.
 Gouvernance mondiale des prix : Gérer les processus internes d’approbation des prix et de gouvernance mondiale pour les actifs attitrés; travailler en étroite collaboration avec l’équipe mondiale de l’Établissement des prix pour assurer l’harmonisation avec les directives mondiales d’établissement des prix et le développement des analyses de rentabilité.
 Soutien relatif au CEPMB : Appuyer les obligations de déclaration auprès du CEPMB et toute enquête sur d’éventuels revenus excessifs, en fournissant des données et des analyses sur les prix.

 Gestion des produits génériques et du cycle de vie : Mettre à jour les scénarios d’impact sur les prix lors du lancement de produits génériques et collaborer avec les Finances à l’évaluation de l’incidence sur les prévisions.

 Collaboration : Travailler de façon interfonctionnelle avec l’Accès au marché, l’Économie de la santé, les Finances, les Affaires juridiques, l’équipe mondiale et les Opérations, et établir des relations de travail positives avec les fonctions internes et les bureaux mondiaux et régionaux d’AbbVie; respecter les transferts de dossiers, les décisions et les échéances; contribuer aux outils, aux processus et aux pratiques exemplaires d’établissement des prix communs à tous les ST, et appuyer ses collègues durant les périodes de pointe.

 Au moins 3 ans d’expérience dans l’industrie pharmaceutique en établissement des prix, en accès au marché, en finances commerciales ou en stratégie.
 Connaissance fonctionnelle du contexte canadien de l’établissement des prix et du remboursement, y compris le CEPMB, l’Alliance pancanadienne pharmaceutique (APP) et les payeurs publics et privés; compréhension de la dynamique des produits génériques et biosimilaires.

 Communications écrites et orales concises et de haute qualité, qui mettent l’accent sur les points clés et créent un lien avec les parties prenantes.

In 1954, Eero Saarinen designed a branch office with glass walls, no offices, and a completely open floor plan in Columbus, Indiana. It was surrounded by trees; the furniture was made by Herman Miller; the lobby flooring was thick, rustic brick. It was built with transparency and community at its core. Since then, a lot of things have happened — Saarinen's branch is now a conference center, people increasingly live on the internet, and it's hard to think of a single financial institution that still applies design thinking to their company.
 Mercury is on a mission to defy those expectations. We're a financial technology company that helps startups spend less time banking* and more time building. We believe that the key to our success revolves around thoughtful design — and we hold the craft of that design to an exceptionally high standard. We're looking for a Staff Brand Designer who sets that bar: someone whose eye is so precise, and whose execution is so considered, that the work around them gets better just by virtue of their presence.
 This is a role for a designer who sweats the details that most people don't notice — the type hierarchy, the negative space, the grid, the crop. Someone who has developed a genuine aesthetic philosophy over years of doing hard work at a high level, and who brings that philosophy to everything they touch. You'll own the most technically complex brand design work at Mercury, provide craft oversight across the Brand Studio, and help define what visual excellence looks like as our brand continues to evolve.

 Set and uphold the craft standard for Mercury's brand — across campaigns, web, social, events, and every surface the brand touches.
 Lead the most technically complex and high-visibility brand design projects end-to-end, from brief through delivery.
 Partner with a staff-level brand designer and creative leadership to co-lead the evolution of Mercury's creative direction — defining and executing visual standards across typography, imagery, layout, and motion.
 Provide hands-on craft oversight across Brand Studio output — reviewing work, raising the quality floor, and helping the team make better decisions.
 Commission and art-direct external creatives: photographers, illustrators, and motion designers.
 Develop brand system documentation and decision-making frameworks that help the team move with confidence and consistency.
 Mentor IC3 and IC4 designers through critique, pairing, and direct feedback — elevating their craft through the work, not just in conversation.
 Collaborate with brand strategists, copywriters, PMMs, and leadership on how Mercury shows up across all channels.
 Shape how Brand Studio uses AI in its craft. You’ll set the standard for where AI belongs in the creative process, build AI-ready brand guidelines the team can design against, and hold the quality bar as these tools become part of how work gets made.
 What you’ll bring:
 A portfolio that is simply excellent — work that demonstrates mastery of typography, layout, color, and composition across a range of brand contexts.
 A clear and deeply held aesthetic point of view: you can articulate what makes something great and what makes something fall short, and you've built that perspective through years of rigorous practice.

The Role 
 BeyondTrust is a global leader in privileged access management. Our products provide remote access and privileged control capabilities that are deployed across thousands of enterprise environments worldwide. That makes us a high-value target. Nation-state actors, ransomware operators, and sophisticated threat groups actively target companies like ours—not just to compromise our corporate environment, but to reach the customers who trust our software to protect their most sensitive systems. A compromise of BeyondTrust is a compromise of the privileged access layer inside our customers’ networks. We take that responsibility seriously.
 As a Cyber Defense Engineer on our Cyber Defense Operations team, you will serve as a front-line defender responsible for protecting both BeyondTrust’s enterprise infrastructure and the integrity of the products our customers depend on. You will monitor, investigate, and respond to security events in an environment where the stakes are real and the adversaries are capable. You will work alongside experienced threat hunters, incident responders, and detection engineers in a collaborative team that values sharp analytical thinking over checkbox compliance.
 This team is building toward an AI-augmented operating model. You will be expected to use AI-driven tools in your daily work and to contribute to how we integrate these capabilities into our detection, triage, and response workflows. We are not looking for people who are waiting to be told what to do—we are looking for people who want to build something.
 What You’ll Do 
 Alert Triage & Monitoring 
 Monitor and triage security alerts across SIEM, EDR, and CSPM platforms covering both corporate and product environments.
 Investigate alerts to determine scope, severity, and whether escalation is warranted.
 Leverage AI-assisted triage and enrichment tools to accelerate analysis and reduce mean time to detect.
 Classify, document, and track alerts through the full lifecycle using ticketing and case management systems.
 Incident Response & Investigation 
 Participate in or lead incident response engagements from detection through remediation, including evidence collection, forensic analysis, root cause determination, and stakeholder communication.
 Conduct investigations across SIEM, EDR, CSPM, and cloud-native log sources including identity provider logs, cloud audit trails, and network flow data—spanning both corporate and product infrastructure.
 Execute established IR runbooks across identity, endpoint, cloud, and email investigation workflows.
 Manage or assist with evidence handling, forensic artifact collection, and chain-of-custody procedures.
 Produce clear, decision-ready incident summaries and post-incident reports for both technical and leadership audiences.
 Detection Engineering & Threat Intelligence 
 Contribute to the design, implementation, and tuning of detection rules across SIEM and EDR platforms, with a focus on reducing false positives and closing coverage gaps.
 Translate threat intelligence (CVE advisories, CISA alerts, vendor bulletins, open-source feeds) into actionable detection content, with particular attention to threats targeting privileged access tooling and supply chain attack vectors.
 Help maintain and evolve detection coverage mapped to MITRE ATT&CK.
 Partner with threat hunting peers to validate detection logic through hypothesis-driven hunts.
 AI Integration & Automation 
 Use AI-driven tools for alert triage, enrichment, and investigation as a standard part of daily operations.
 Contribute to the evaluation, integration, and optimization of AI and automation capabilities across the team’s workflows.
 Assist in designing prompts, agent workflows, or LLM-based pipelines that augment analyst capabilities and reduce manual effort.

MongoDB powers mission‑critical workloads for customers who expect their data to be durable, highly available, and fast to access. The Storage Execution team builds the core infrastructure that makes those guarantees real.
 We are hiring a Senior Engineering Manager to manage the largely New York-based Storage Execution team. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is obsessed with customer success, takes the responsibility of durably storing customer data seriously, and has strong empathy for both their team and our users.
 This role can be based remotely in Ontario, Canada.
 About the Storage Execution team
 The Storage Execution team sits at the heart of MongoDB’s Online Transaction Processing (OLTP) team. We own the core transactional read/write path on each node, across both today’s storage engine and a next‑generation cloud-native storage architecture. Our work determines how correct and performant MongoDB is for customers running mission-critical production workloads.
 The team’s responsibilities include:
 Defining and maintaining the internal collection and index APIs used by Replication, Query and Catalog modules, and commands for local reads and writes, plus the transaction and durability primitives that govern visibility, conflict resolution and crash recovery
 Integrating the next generation of MongoDB’s storage architecture into the server in a way that is predictable for other teams, scales with cloud elasticity, and preserves the performance and safety of the classic configuration
 Improving transaction processing speed and semantics of both single shard and cross-shard transactions
 Owning index builds and schema‑level storage operations (build/rebuild, cleanup, resumability) and ensuring they behave well for large, highly available clusters running write-heavy workloads
 Building validation, diagnostics, and storage‑focused test infrastructure to catch durability issues early and keep the system trustworthy at scale
 Partnering with neighboring teams on flow control, prioritization and load-shedding to stay within resource limits, protecting durability and availability at the cluster level without starving critical operations
 What you’ll do
 Lead, grow and manage a New York–based team of 8 to 10 engineers; ensure clear expectations, high standards, and healthy, sustainable execution
 Own the team’s roadmap across durability, availability, performance, and developer productivity, in partnership with OLTP leadership and Product Management
 Manage customer escalations involving storage behavior and durability; work directly with Support, Atlas, and other server teams to reproduce, root‑cause, and resolve issues
 Drive process and tooling improvements that raise engineering velocity and code quality (e.g., ownership, review expectations, customer escalation and build failure practices)
 Partner closely with Replication, Query, Sharding, Catalog & Routing, Storage Engines, and Atlas teams on cross‑team features such as the new storage architecture, availability improvements, and workload management
 Represent Storage Execution in planning, staffing, and calibration; make thoughtful tradeoffs between near‑term deliverables, longer‑term availability gaps, and platform investments
 Candidate profile
 8+ years building, debugging, and tuning distributed and/or highly concurrent systems software (databases, storage engines, filesystems, or similar)
 2+ years managing engineers directly, including hiring, performance management, and coaching across a range of levels
 Willing to work East Coast hours
 Strong proficiency in at least one compiled, statically-typed language such as C++, Rust, or Go; prior C++ and systems programming experience is a plus
 Deep understanding of durability, availability, and performance tradeoffs in distributed systems; experience with replication, consensus, storage engines, or transactional systems is highly desirable
 Demonstrated customer obsession: direct experience working with demanding customers (or customer support / cloud teams) on complex incidents and turning them into clear, outcome‑oriented recommendations
 Proven ability to develop people: mentoring and promoting engineers, managing underperformance directly, and building high‑engagement teams with low regretted attrition
 Comfortable leading multi‑quarter initiatives with multiple stakeholders and using written documents to align teams on design, scope, and tradeoffs
 Success measures
 In three months, you have:
 Built strong relationships with your team and key partner teams
 Taken over team ceremonies, short‑term planning, and on‑call responsibilities
 Co‑led at least one active project and shipped one concrete process improvement
 In six to twelve months, you have:
 Led at least one cross‑team initiative in availability, durability, or developer velocity
 Delivered a multi‑quarter project with clear impact on durability/availability or team throughput
 Built a bench of engineers ready for increased scope and, over time, leadership roles

Role context

This role sits on the Product Marketing team and reports to the Director of Product Marketing. You'll be aligned to one or more of our product pillars and work with one to three product managers and their engineers, taking products from alpha through public beta to general availability. You're the translator between what product and engineering build and the language sales and customers use.

The role

You will own how your products reach the market, from first alpha to GA.

 - Plan and run launches for mid-tier (P2) products end to end, and lead a major workstream on our biggest (P1) launches, so sales and customer teams are ready on launch day.

 - Shape messaging, positioning and naming with your product counterpart so technical capabilities land as clear value for both the buyer and the frontline technician.

 - Build the collateral, video scripts and enablement that help reps close faster and help customers adopt what we ship.

 - Partner with Demand Gen on campaign messaging and review what goes to market.

 - Use analytics tools, customer conversations and market research to understand buyers, and own an adoption goal, shared with your product counterpart, that we review every week.

Within six to twelve months, product, sales and marketing should see you as the person to ask about your products. You'll have real autonomy to set strategy with your product counterpart and bring recommendations to your manager. Your priorities will shift each quarter with what the business needs.

About you

Must-haves

 - 2–4 years in product marketing or a closely related role, such as sales enablement, sales or marketing

 - You've taken a product launch from plan to release and can tell us what worked and what didn't

 - You write clearly and present with confidence to sales, product and executive audiences

 - You've worked with go-to-market teams before and after the sale

 - You're comfortable getting hands-on in tools like Tableau, Databricks and Salesforce to check on customers and adoption

 - You see the whole picture: tell you one thing and you can map the many moving parts behind it

 - You welcome feedback, take accountability, and know when to push and when to agree and move on

Nice-to-haves

 - Background in manufacturing, industrial or other asset-intensive industries

 - Experience marketing B2B software or AI products

We offer

Your work shows up in the physical world. What we ship keeps factories, fleets and campuses running, and when it works, a technician goes home on time. You're joining a product the industry already loves, now part of Autodesk, with the scale of a global public company pointed at the problem we were already solving. The seat is early, not inherited: the team is small enough that you can name the parts of the launch process you own. And operations is new ground inside Autodesk, so the people who join now have real room to grow.

Values and how we work

We reward output and promote quickly when people deliver. Product marketing here means navigating strong opinions from product, sales and marketing, because everyone cares about the work. We look for people who are smart, humble and optimistic: open to feedback, easy to work with, and honest about what didn't go to plan.

Our clients include corporate security teams around the world, including some of the world’s leading organizations.  Liferaft was recently acquired by global security company Securitas, expanding our ability to deliver intelligence-led security at scale.  Liferaft is looking for a highly skilled and visionary Senior Product Manager to play a crucial role in shaping the future of our OSINT solutions. This role will be hybrid in Halifax, NS, or fully remote within the Eastern, or Atlantic time zones in Canada. 
 Reporting to the Chief Innovation Officer, You will be responsible for defining product strategy, collaborating with cross-functional teams, and driving the development of innovative intelligence tools that address our customers' most critical needs. This role requires a deep understanding of OSINT methodologies, strong analytical skills, and the ability to translate complex requirements into user-centric solutions.

 Product Line Strategy & Vision: Define and communicate a compelling product roadmap aligned with company goals and market needs.

 5+ years of product management experience, preferably in the OSINT, cybersecurity, intelligence, or data analytics space.
